activities.caption: rebuild the hierarchy, best option first
activities.name: wceHierarchyOrder

config.prompt: The five tiers, most environmentally valuable first:
config.why: Reuse keeps a product's embodied value intact for dozens of trips; recycling spends energy and degrades quality; energy-from-waste beats landfill's methane release but loses to any reuse — and landfill is the floor.

activities.anchor: Run one decision through the hierarchy with numbers
activities.caption: one container, three lives — pair each route with its energy story
activities.name: wceContainerMatch

config.prompt: One drink container, several destinies — pair the route with its energy story:

pairs.right: amortises its making energy over dozens of trips — beats both recycle routes if collection works
saves about 25–30% of its making energy per loop
recycles once, at moderate saving, into lower-grade fibre before dropping out of the loop
industrialises the top of the ranking — collection rates above 90% where run well

config.why: The ranking that emerges — reuse of durable containers over recycling of singles — is not preference; it is thermodynamics reading a materials table.

activities.caption: file each material by its loop life
activities.name: wceLoopBuckets

config.prompt: How many recycling loops does each material family survive? File them:

items.label: steel — magnetically sorted at massive scale
paper — cellulose fibres shorten each pass
mechanically recycled plastic — chains shorten each loop
glass — cullet lowers the melt temperature

config.why: Only about 9% of all plastic ever made has been recycled; roughly three-quarters of all aluminium ever made is still in service — the difference is polymer chemistry versus metal re-melting.

activities.anchor: The label describes a requirement, not a guarantee
activities.caption: bet before you read on — the compostable cup
activities.name: wceCupPredict

config.q: A compostable coffee cup is tossed into a landfill. What happens to it?
choices: It composts — that is what the label promises
Almost nothing — a landfill is anaerobic and dry, so the cup mummifies
It dissolves into the leachate harmlessly
config.why: A compostable cup composts nothing in a dry, airless landfill — and in the recycling stream it would contaminate a plastics batch it was never designed to join. Compostability is an infrastructure claim first, a materials claim second.

activities.anchor: the fastest-growing and most paradoxical stream
activities.caption: put the e-waste stream on the scale
activities.name: wceEwastePlace

config.prompt: E-waste — the fastest-growing waste stream — runs about how many million tonnes a year?
config.why: About 60 million tonnes a year, rich in gold, cobalt, palladium and rare earths — one tonne of circuit boards holds more gold than a tonne of gold ore, alongside lead, mercury and flame retardants.
config.context: Formal urban mining recovers the value; informal burning in Agbogbloshie and Guiyu delivers the poison.

activities.caption: the carpet company's business model — trace each path
activities.name: wceCarpetBranch

config.root: You run an office-carpet company and the board wants a strategy for the next decade.

start.text: How do you sell floor covering?

choices.label: Sell carpet, cheapest per square metre
choices.feedback: The linear playbook — and its logic starts working against you.

choices.label: Lease floor-service and reclaim every tile
choices.feedback: Product-as-service — the maker keeps ownership of the materials.

choices.label: Sell carpet with a recycling promise, design unchanged
choices.feedback: A bin-colour strategy: the promise collides with the product architecture.

linear.text: Replacement is your growth engine, so durability becomes the enemy. Adhesive-fixed mixed tiles go to landfill, and the demolition cost lands on someone else's ledger.

service.text: Interface's case: suddenly durability and repairability serve the seller instead of undermining it. The tiles come back, and the materials keep their value.

promise.text: Recycling cost is set at the drawing board — laminates and adhesives decide it. 'Recyclable' on the label stays aspiration until the infrastructure and the design both exist.

config.why: Circularity is an engineering and business-model discipline, not a bin colour — every instrument on the redesign list moves the disposal cost back to the point of design decision.

activities.anchor: The scale numbers frame everything above
activities.caption: call the 2050 curve — municipal waste
activities.name: wceScaleEstimate

config.prompt: The world generates roughly 2 billion tonnes of municipal solid waste a year. On current trends, where does that land by 2050?
config.why: About 3.4 billion tonnes by 2050 — with the growth concentrated exactly where collection is weakest, and about a third of today's waste still openly dumped or burned.
config.context: Per-capita generation tracks income: under 0.5 kg/day in the poorest regions, 1.5–2+ kg/day in the richest — waste is the indicator that tracks the material economy most directly.

activities.caption: true or false — the lifecycle auditor
activities.name: wceLcaJudge

statements.s: Reusable cotton bags beat single-use plastic bags on carbon after just a handful of trips.
statements.why: The break-even is a few dozen reuses — cotton's farming burden pushes it higher still. Honest comparisons cite their break-even uses.

statements.s: A paper bag's carbon per carry often exceeds plastic's.
statements.why: LCA sometimes overturns intuition — the 'right' packaging depends on the metric (carbon, litter, water) and the reuse count.

statements.s: A well-run modern landfill is a lined, engineered containment with leachate collection and gas capture.
statements.why: Its methane can be harvested as fuel; the long-term problem is custody, not chemistry.

statements.s: Waste-to-energy plants are cleaner than open burning and worse than recycling.
statements.why: The hierarchy holds — Denmark's Amager Bakke even doubles as a ski slope, but it sits below reuse and recycling all the same.
